html:
SMTO-TSK-0002 — SMTO tried to ask you a question while doing other things

GUID: 7e4b538d-5902-44d1-a6e4-e8ec4fbfaf4e
Slug: exclusive-user-interaction
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The AI tried to ask you a question and start other actions in the same step. SMTO cancelled that whole step before any of it ran, and normally asks the AI to try again by itself.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment. SMTO usually corrects this by itself, and its question for you then appears on its own. SMTO tells the AI to ask the question alone first, then carry on with your answer.
  2. When a question appears, answer it before adding new instructions. The work that depends on your reply can only continue once you've answered.
  3. If the task stops with this message, send a message asking SMTO to continue. Nothing from the rejected step ran, so asking SMTO to carry on doesn't repeat any work from that step.
  4. If this happens on many tasks, ask the person who manages SMTO whether a different Main model in Settings › Setup › Model routing would work better. This mistake comes from the AI model, not from how you worded your request.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows its question by itself, or the task carries on without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. You don't need to change your request; this comes from the AI model.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model decision combined ask_user or request_resource_access with other tool calls in one batch; the whole decision was rejected before any of its calls ran.

What this means

  • A model decision combines ask_user with other tool calls in the same batch, violating the exclusive interaction boundary. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A model decision combines ask_user with other tool calls in the same batch, violating the exclusive interaction boundary.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the decision's call list; ask_user must be the sole call for that interaction.

How to fix it

  • turn_dispatch._dispatch_decision rejects any decision with more than one tool call that includes ask_user or request_resource_access, records an executed=false error for every call and charges metadata_miss; after the metadata retry limit the run stops as partial. Submit ask_user alone and use the accepted answer in a later decision; review the Main model's tool-call behavior if it recurs.
  • Submit ask_user alone, then use the accepted answer in a later decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A separate accepted interaction receives its answer before dependent actions are proposed.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
